'''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社, also known as '''Rokusha Shrine''' (六社神社)) is a type of {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in Japan. Shrines bearing this name can be found throughout the country.

The shrine's name derives from enshrining six deities. This may have been the case from the time of its founding or due to the merging of six shrines for practical reasons.

Some of the {{ill|Sōja|ar|سوجا (أوكاياما)|azb|سوجا، اوکایاما|ce|Содзя|ceb|Sōja|de|Sōja|el|Σότζα|es|Sōja (Okayama)|fa|سوجا، اوکایاما|fi|Sōja|fr|Sōja|gl|Sōja|ha|Sōja|id|Sōja, Okayama|it|Sōja|ja|総社市|ko|소자시|mg|Sōja|mzn|سوجا، اوکایاما|nl|Soja (Okayama)|pl|Sōja|pt|Soja (Okayama)|ro|Sōja|ru|Содзя|sv|Sōja, Okayama|tg|Соҷа|th|โซจะ|tl|Sōja|tr|Sōja|tt|Содзя|tum|Sōja|uk|Соджя|ur|سوجا|vi|Sōja, Okayama|war|Sōja, Okayama|zh|總社市|zh_classical|總社市|zh_min_nan|Sôzya-chhī|zh_yue|總社|qid=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} (総社, provincial shrines) in the [[Ritsuryō system|Ritsuryō period]] bear the name "Rokusho Shrine" or "Rokusho-no-Miya." These served as sōja by enshrining deities from the [[Ichinomiya]] to the Rokunomiya of the province. Historian [[Yoshida Tōgo]] argued that "Rokusho" not only means "six places" but also signifies a "registry office" for managing and overseeing shrines in the jurisdiction. Folklorist [[Nakayama Tarō]] proposed that "registry office" could imply a connection to burial grounds.<ref>{{Cite book|和書
